name: Victor Sun
life: “I used to check other people's scales using a little weight in my pocket.” On Monday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Victor takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I want to measure myself again. Chemotherapy stole a little of my height and a lot of my nerve.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a faded indigo overshirt and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. Victor has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with tightly curled gray hair. Victor leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Victor can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To add one present-day height mark after treatment.
family: Cato Hull is Victor’s younger relative by marriage. Victor is free to hang up first. Cato makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Cato says, “On my break I taught three children how water moves around a pier.”
connections: Stefan Tate. A new adult height mark fits beside names the former childminder still remembers.

reactions.situation: The landlord wants the height marks covered today
reactions.response: Victor offers to help trace the height marks before work continues.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Victor draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Victor asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
